Tips & troubleshooting
  • Only the first launch needs internet — the face-tracking model (~10 MB) is downloaded once and saved on this PC, so later launches load it from disk. (A couple of small runtime files, ~3 MB, still come from a CDN but are kept in the normal browser cache.)
  • Keep this window visible (a small window snapped to the side is fine). Browsers throttle minimized tabs, which slows detection.
  • False alerts when glancing at a second monitor or keyboard → raise the head-turn or eyes-down threshold, or lengthen the trigger delay.
  • Misses your phone glances → lower the thresholds. The Head off-axis and Eyes-down Δ readouts show live values, so you can see what a phone glance scores and set thresholds just below it.
  • Camera won’t start from a double-clicked file → use Chrome or Edge; if it still refuses, run python -m http.server in the file’s folder and open localhost:8000/eyes-front.html.
  • Everything runs on your machine — no video or images are uploaded anywhere.
